prompt.context: Our client is Excavator Mining Co, a large diversified mining company. Excavator is considering developing a mine site to produce copper ore. Excavator has two options for developing the site: develop alone, or enter a joint venture (JV) with a competitor, Drillhammer Mining Co. In addition, Drillhammer owns a nearby mining site which it could develop to produce copper ore, supplying the same market.
prompt.question: Should Excavator develop the mine alone, with Drillhammer, or not at all? What arrangements should be made with Drillhammer, if any?

clarifying_info.q: What is the capacity and mine life for each option?
clarifying_info.a: Excavator alone: 1 million tonnes per year, 20-year mine life. Drillhammer alone: 1 million tonnes per year, 20-year mine life. JV at Excavator site: 2 million tonnes per year, 20-year mine life.

clarifying_info.q: What is the copper ore price?
What are the operating costs for each option?
clarifying_info.a: Excavator alone: mining $20/t, rail transport $10/t, road transport $5/t, total $35/t. Drillhammer alone: mining $28/t, rail to link $8/t, road transport $25/t - but interviewer should provide the exhibit. JV at Excavator site: mining $15/t, rail $5/t, road $5/t, total $30/t.

clarifying_info.q: What are the capital investments required?
Should we use discounted cash flows or ignore time value of money?
clarifying_info.a: Ignore time value of money for this analysis.

clarifying_info.q: Why is the JV mine production larger than Excavator alone?
clarifying_info.a: This can be attributed to capital requirements for Excavator alone, or regulatory reasons.

exhibits.title: Site Overview
exhibits.shows: A map/diagram showing the geographic layout: Excavator-owned site, Drillhammer-owned site, a rail link, road from mine to market, and the copper ore market. Annotations show capacity and mine life for each site option.
exhibits.data: Excavator site: 1M tonnes pa standalone, 2M tonnes pa under JV, 20-year mine life. Drillhammer site: 1M tonnes pa, 20-year mine life. Infrastructure: rail link, road from rail link to market, road from mine to market.

exhibits.title: Mine Financial Assessment
exhibits.shows: A financial comparison table across three scenarios: Excavator alone, Drillhammer alone, and JV at Excavator site. Shows capacity, mine life, copper ore price, itemised operating costs, operating profit per tonne, total profit over mine life, capital investment, and total value.
exhibits.data: Capacity: 1,000,000 / 1,000,000 / 2,000,000 tonnes pa. Mine life: 20 / 20 / 20 years. Copper ore price: $50/t all. Mining costs: $20.0 / $28.0 / $15.0 per tonne. Rail transport (Drillhammer to link / JV): $0.0 / $8.0 / $5.0 per tonne. Road transport: $10.0 / $10.0 (rail link to market) / n/a; road $5.0 / $25.0 / $5.0. Total operating costs: $35.0 / $53.0 / $30.0 per tonne. Operating profit: $15.0 / ($3.0) / $20.0 per tonne. Total profit over mine life: $300M / ($60M) / $800M. Capital investment: ($180M) / ($140M) / ($340M). Total value: $120M / ($200M) / $460M.

framework: Evaluate financial attractiveness of each of the three options: Excavator alone, Drillhammer alone, and JV at Excavator site
Calculate operating profit per tonne = price - total operating costs for each scenario
Calculate total profit over mine life = operating profit per tonne x capacity x mine life
Calculate total value = total profit over mine life - capital investment
Determine each party's best alternative (BATNA) if no JV
Negotiate JV value split: divide incremental JV value equally above each party's BATNA
Discuss qualitative considerations and broader strategic factors

questions.prompt: Calculate the total value for each of the three scenarios (Excavator alone, Drillhammer alone, JV).
questions.guidance: Candidate should walk through: (1) operating profit per tonne = price minus total costs, (2) total profit = op profit x volume x years, (3) total value = total profit minus capex. Key insight: Drillhammer alone is loss-making; JV creates the highest total value at $460M.

math.setup: For each scenario: Total Value = (Price - Total OpEx) x Capacity x Mine Life - Capex

questions.prompt: Given the financial analysis, which option creates the most value and why would Drillhammer participate in the JV?
questions.guidance: JV at Excavator site creates $460M total value, the highest of all options. Drillhammer alone is loss-making (-$200M total value), so Drillhammer would not invest in its own site. The JV is the only way Drillhammer can create positive value. Excavator alone yields $120M, but JV creates far more value for the industry overall.

questions.prompt: How should the JV value of $460M be split between Excavator and Drillhammer?
questions.guidance: Use BATNA logic: without the JV, Drillhammer earns $0 (won't invest in its loss-making site) and Excavator earns $120M. Total without JV = $120M. The JV adds $460M - $120M = $340M of incremental value. This $340M should be split evenly between the two parties. Each gets $170M of incremental value. Drillhammer: $0 + $170M = $170M. Excavator: $120M + $170M = $290M. A straight 50/50 split of $460M ($230M each) is not fair to Excavator since it gives up its $120M standalone option.

math.setup: Incremental JV value = JV total value - sum of BATNAs. Split incremental value equally.
steps: BATNA: Excavator alone = $120M; Drillhammer alone (won't invest) = $0
math.answer: Drillhammer should receive $170M; Excavator should receive $290M. Excavator should not accept less than $290M.

brainstorming.prompt: What other qualitative or strategic factors should be considered in the JV decision and arrangement?

categories.name: JV relationship factors
ideas: History of prior JVs or partnerships between Excavator and Drillhammer
Cultural and operational compatibility between the two companies
Governance structure and decision-making rights in the JV

categories.name: Alternatives and optionality
ideas: Alternative uses for Drillhammer's mine site - could it be sold?
Could Excavator acquire Drillhammer's site outright instead of a JV?
Potential for infrastructure sharing between the two sites (rail, roads)

categories.name: Market and pricing risk
ideas: Copper ore price over a 20-year horizon is highly uncertain
At what price would Drillhammer's standalone site become profitable?
How does a higher or lower copper price affect the JV vs standalone decision?

categories.name: Regulatory and operational risk
ideas: Operational risks of running a 2M tonne pa operation vs 1M tonne pa

recommendation: Excavator should pursue the JV with Drillhammer at Excavator's mine site
The JV creates $460M in total value vs $120M for Excavator alone, generating $340M of incremental industry value
Excavator should negotiate for no less than $290M of the JV value (its BATNA of $120M plus half the incremental $340M)
risks: Copper ore prices could fall over the 20-year mine life, reducing or eliminating profitability
JV governance and operational disputes with Drillhammer could erode value
Drillhammer may have alternative options not identified in this analysis
next_steps: Conduct sensitivity analysis on copper ore price assumptions over 20 years
Investigate JV governance structures and negotiate terms to protect Excavator's interests
Confirm no superior alternative use for either mine site exists
Assess infrastructure sharing opportunities between the two sites
